caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 157 of 1996.
lawyer:
Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Sajjadul Huq, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioner. 
Mokbul Ahmed, Advocate instructed by Md Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record — For the Respondent No. 1. 
Not represented — Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Jainab Begum ----- 2nd Party-Petitioner
vs.  
Md Abu Taher & anr ----- 1st Party-Respondents
full_judgment:
Mohammad Abdur Rouf J: Upon an application, filed by 1st party-respondent No. 1, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong by his order dated 13-5-92 drew up a proceeding under section 145 CrPC against the petitioner and respondent No. 2, Misc. Case No. 202 of 1992, in respect of the proceeding property, which is a semi pucca shop room belonging to the petitioner. The Officer-in-Charge of Kotwali Police Station was directed to maintain peace thereat and to submit a report by 15-6-92. 

 3. The petitioner appeared in the case and filed an application praying for attachment of the proceeding shop room and appointment of a receiver. The Magistrate on 29-6-93 rejected her petition. On 4-12-93 the petitioner again filed an application for attachment of the property and appointment of a receiver alleging, inter alia, that 1st party-respondent No.1 had stopped payment of rent for the proceeding shop room since July, 1991 and without her consent he sub-let the same to one Abdus Sabur who along with his relation, present respondent No. 2, Dil Mohammad Khan started running a business in the proceeding room under the name and style "Banskhali Hotel" and that said Dil Mohammd, however, subsequently entered into a Bharanama agreement with the petitioner. But respondent No.1 all on a sudden on 18-5-92 forcibly entered into the hotel and dispossessed Dil Mohammad therefrom and changed the signboard of the hotel and put up a new signboard as "Abu Taher Hotel" and that over the incident both respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed a case and counter-case against each other, being Kotwali PS Case No. 24(5)92 and 29(5) 92 respectively and that an apprehension of serious breach of peace had been prevailing in respect of the said property which might lead to cause damage to the same. 

 4. After hearing the parties the concerned Magistrate by his order dated 8-12-93 allowed the petition, attached the property and appointed the officer-in-charge, Kotwali Police Station as the receiver. The learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong in Criminal Motion No. 786 of 1993, preferred by respondent No. 1, by his judgment and order dated 10-7-94 upheld the order of the Magistrate. Against that order respondent No. 1 preferred Criminal Misc. Case No. 2038 of 1994 under section 561A CrPC before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dated 22-5-96 allowed the said Misc. Case making the Rule absolute and set aside the order passed by the courts below. Second party No. 1 petitioner is now seeking leave to appeal from the said judgment of the High Court Division. 

 5. Mr Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the petitioner's reasonable apprehension of causing damage by respondent Nos. 1 and 2 to her valuable property, have wrongly set aside the order of the Magistrate regarding attachment of the property and appointment of the receiver.
